text.p: The Italian debt market saw timid positive signals with the June Bpt Liffe future ending firmer but off session highs, but a mood of caution prevailed.
The June Btp finished 61 basis points firmer at 127.10, at one point breaching resistance at 127.20/35 to reach a day's high at 127.49.

"The rebound today is only a recovery from an excessive fall which had especially penalised the Italian market," one operator said. A firmer lira against the mark helped sentiment, however, helped by reported Bank of Italy lira buying for marks and dollars. The lira was firmer at a late 991.90/2.20.

U.S. Treasuries were steady after factory orders data with few willing to take out new positions ahead of Friday's payrolls report. Traders said a drop in weekly jobless claims pointed to a labour market remaining tight.
Italian dealers said European markets were still likely to suffer from prospects for a single European currency.
"Today there was no negative news on EMU and this calmed the market," one dealer said. "The debate on the single currency is being used in Germany for domestic political aims," another commented.
The spread over 10-year bunds narrowed to 184 bps.
